v.why: Restoring a missing input-to-output residual path in conv-heavy cells gave large gains (#51,#52,#54,#55,#60), but swapping a conv or pool for a skip gave only small gains (#56-58).
Replacing the residual skip on edge 3 with a conv usually hurt (#1-4,#7), but filling an empty or pooled edge 3 helped or was neutral (#8,#9).
With edge 4 removed, the cell is shallow and has few paths to the output, so adding conv capacity on edge 3 helps a lot (#5,#6) instead of hurting (#1-4).
When edge 4 is already absent, removing edge 5 cuts the main conv route into the output node, which was catastrophic (#83,#84,#90) compared with the milder losses elsewhere.
With edge 1 absent, node 2 can only be reached through edge 0, so removing edge 0 disconnects the deep paths (#25,#30).
Without the residual edge 3, deepening edge 0 makes optimization harder and was harmful (#96,#100), but with a skip on edge 3 the same edit helped (#91-99).
Adding depth on edge 5 in a cell with no residual edge 3 hurt (#20), while the same edit was positive in cells that have the skip (#11-19).
If edge 5 is missing, filling edge 4 restores a parametric path into the output, giving large gains (#77) instead of marginal ones (#71-75).
When edge 0 is absent, node 1 is dead, so edge 1 is the only input to node 2 and adding a conv there gave large gains (#68) compared with roughly neutral effects (#61-67).
When the node-2 inputs are weak non-parametric pools, a conv on edge 5 adds needed learnable capacity (#14, and the analogous #69) compared with conv-fed node 2 (#11,#16-19).

raw:
Ten hypotheses follow, based on the 100 experiments and on how NAS-Bench-201 cells are wired. Most rest on one to five supporting experiments, so they are leads to test, not established effects. Two patterns dominate:

- **Bottleneck effect:** an edit has a much larger effect when the parent cell has few working paths into node 3, for example when e3 or e4 is `none`.
- **Skip-edge effect:** adding a convolution where e3 is currently a `skip_connect` usually hurts, because it removes the identity path from input to output.
